subject: 🔬 Anthropic pays $500K/yr for safety research, no ML needed
intro: AI is quietly eating its own job description. Google's ScientistTwo now writes better ML papers than humans. Anthropic is paying up to $500K to recruit physicists and founders into safety research, no ML background needed. The throughline? The bottleneck is no longer compute or models. It's people who understand what to do with them. We're watching the field recruit faster than it can train, and automate faster than it can recruit.

news.headline: Anthropic opens paid AI safety residency, no ML background needed
news.body: Anthropic just opened a paid research residency, and it is not your typical internship. This is a career pivot program for people who already have serious technical chops but zero AI safety experience. Here is the setup: you have strong skills in some technical field, but AI safety research feels like a locked door. This program is the key. You work on a real scoped research project matched to your background. Shorter placements can be remote. Longer ones prefer San Francisco, with visa sponsorship available. This opens up a path to publish real AI safety research and potentially join Anthropic full-time. Apply by November 22.
bullets: No ML background needed -- they teach you modern machine learning on the job
Placements run 6 weeks to 6 months , full-time
Pay is $350K to $500K annualized , prorated to your placement length
You get a dedicated Anthropic mentor, GPU compute budget, and access to Claude models
Research areas include interpretability, AI control, scalable oversight, and red-teaming

news.headline: Anthropic's Claude API now caches conversations server-side, cutting time to first token by 35%
news.body: Every turn in a long AI conversation, your app was resending the entire chat history to the server. Every. Single. Turn. For a coding agent running hundreds of requests, that ballooned to around 800 KB per request . Anthropic just fixed that with Message Threads, now in public beta on the Messages API. The server stores your conversation between turns. You send only new messages plus the previous response ID, and Claude starts replying faster. That 800 KB request? It drops to 1.8 KB . One catch: threads can expire, so you still need to keep your own conversation history locally as a backup. The bigger your context, the more you gain from this.
bullets: Median time before Claude starts responding drops by 35% on requests with 500K to 1M tokens
Threads are encrypted in memory, never written to disk, and expire 5 minutes after the last request
To use it: add the thread parameter and beta header to your API requests
No extra cost, standard token rates apply

news.headline: Claude generates a Studio Ghibli anime scene as a single HTML file with no assets
news.body: Fable 5.5 just one-shotted a full anime short film. No video model. No assets. Pure code. Someone gave it a detailed Studio Ghibli-style prompt and it spat out a single self-contained HTML file with a giant robot waking up in a mossy forest, rising into a golden sky. The whole thing runs in your browser with zero dependencies. Here is what the file actually does: The kicker? No image or video model was involved. Fable 5.5 wrote every frame procedurally in code. You can clone the repo at ChetasLua/moss-keeper, open index.html, and it works offline instantly. Run the same prompt on Fable 5.1 and quality drops noticeably. This shows how fast the gap between model versions is growing for creative code tasks.
bullets: Film embedded as base64 MP4, decoded into a Blob at load time
Custom player with play/pause, seek bar, fullscreen, and sound toggle
Live film-grain overlay drawn on a Canvas element
Keyboard shortcuts built in: Space, arrow keys, M, F
